headline: The IGF-1 ceiling
punch: It is far lower than you think.

headline: Everyone online pushes it up
body: So the logic in every protocol is to push IGF-1 as high as you can tolerate, on the assumption that the number tracks how much growing you are doing. Meanwhile the people who prescribe growth hormone for a living run a hard ceiling on exactly that number and titrate the dose down to stay under it. | Those two approaches cannot both be right, and only one of them has a published figure behind it. So it is worth knowing what that ceiling is and what it is actually for.
punch: There is a published ceiling. It is low.

headline: How low is the ceiling?
body: The standing recommendation is that IGF-1 levels **should not exceed 2 SDS**, because of concerns about increasing the potential risk of adverse events. | SDS means standard deviation score: how far above the mean you sit, for your age and sex. Two SDS is the top edge of the normal range. It is not a supraphysiological target that clinicians are aiming at, it is the line they are trying to stay underneath while still getting an effect.
punch: ==The clinical ceiling is the top of normal.==

headline: The Swedish guideline
body: The 2020 Swedish national guidelines give the whole structure in one sentence: a standard GH dose of **33 µg per kg per day** adjusted for IGF-1, with an **upper limit below 2 SDS**. And in the first two years of treatment, an IGF-1 up to **3 SDS can be short-term tolerated** if necessary. | So there is a small amount of headroom early in treatment, and it is explicitly described as temporary rather than as a target.
punch: A dose, then a number that caps the dose.

headline: So what is IGF-1 for?
body: Here is the part that gets completely inverted online. The recommended use of IGF-1 is as a **long-term safety marker** for patients on GH. It exists to catch overshoot, not to measure progress. | And an optimal IGF-1 target for long-term height outcomes **has not yet been established**. There is no validated number to aim at, which means anyone telling you to hit a specific IGF-1 figure for growth has invented that figure.
punch: _It is a brake, not an accelerator._

headline: Dose and number drift apart
body: In that cohort, samples at or above 2 SDS came from a median GH dose of **0.042 mg/kg/day** against **0.038** for samples below it. P < 0.001, so a real difference. | But look at the ranges rather than the medians: 0.02 to 0.10 against 0.01 to 0.10. They overlap almost completely. What this means is that nearly the same dose lands all over the IGF-1 range depending entirely on who is taking it.
punch: The same dose gives wildly different numbers.

headline: Puberty moves it too
body: In the same samples, the high IGF-1 group had **lower** estradiol in girls, 13 against 102 pmol/L, and **lower** testosterone in boys, 0.35 against 6.9 nmol/L. Both at P < 0.001. | So where you are in puberty shifts the IGF-1 you get out of a given dose, and shifts it hard. The number is reading your pubertal stage and your hepatic insulin exposure at the same time as it reads your dose.
punch: Your IGF-1 is not a clean readout of your dose.

headline: What to do with the number
body: The ceiling clinicians use is 2 SDS, briefly 3 in the first two years, and it exists for safety rather than for effect. There is no established IGF-1 target for height outcomes at all. | And because the same dose produces very different numbers depending on the person and their pubertal stage, treating that result as a score is reading noise and calling it progress.
punch: ==2 SDS is a brake. There is no target to chase.==
